A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LVLM hallucination-mitigation study, despite changes to the title, framework name and positional module. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, experiments and displays can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original POPE, CHAIR and MME experiments, component ablations, inference measurements and GPT-4o evaluations.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark and ablation results, including additional backbone evaluations, MMBench scores and positional-bias measurements. Retained original results also qualify.

M1.justification: Section 3.2.2 replaces CDAR's uniform image-token positions and weighted attention blending in the first l layers with CMPC's scaled position indices and direct replacement of cross-modal attention logits. This materially changes an inference component. The CMVED-to-IMD renaming largely preserves the value-distortion mechanism.

E1.justification: v3 adds an actual MMBench general-ability evaluation on LLaVA-1.5 (Appendix A, Table 10). POPE's COCO/A-OKVQA/GQA coverage, COCO captioning and MME remain. Additional model backbones expand configurations rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The primary POPE comparison expands beyond standard decoding, VCD and ICD to include PAI and OPERA; OPERA participates only in the greedy setting (v3 Table 1). Conversely, the revised alpha sensitivity experiment drops the VCD comparator present in v2 Table 10.

E3.justification: v3 adds greedy-decoding evaluations, Qwen-VL experiments and LLaVA-OneVision testing. The stated alpha changes from 3 for POPE and 1 elsewhere to 3 generally. POPE reporting adds cross-dataset averages, and component ablations shift from COCO-popular to aggregated POPE-popular. These are substantive configuration and evaluation-design changes.

E4.justification: v3 adds hallucination frequency by image-token position (Table 6), individual-head attention visualizations and global-position-calibration/EOS controls (Table 13). It revises alpha and gamma sensitivity studies while removing the early-layer-count sweep and separate component timing comparison. GPT-4o evaluations and qualitative caption examples are retained.

E5.justification: v3 Section 4.3 newly states that MME results are averaged over four runs. v2 gives no corresponding run count. This establishes additional statistical reporting, not an increase in runs; no dispersion estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests are supplied.

E6.justification: Numerous benchmark and ablation entries change. For example, LLaVA-1.5 COCO-random POPE accuracy/F1 changes from 88.77/87.59 in v2 Table 1 to 89.23/88.68 in v3 Table 7. v3 also adds greedy, additional-backbone and MMBench results. Some results accompany changed settings and the revised method; the GPT-4o scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 adds a short RoPE relative-position derivation in Appendix B, Equation 14, and revises the positional-calibration equations. The mask inequality changes from below-mean in v2 Equation 7 to above-mean in v3 Equation 8, resolving its disagreement with the retained high-attention masking description.

C1.justification: The positional contribution is redefined from content-driven attention refinement to shrinking image-token positional gaps. Positional bias receives greater prominence in the abstract and introduction, but v2 already claimed to address it. The central claims of training-free hallucination mitigation and broad benchmark effectiveness remain.

C2.justification: v3 introduces a RoPE aliasing/context-length explanation and interprets global position scaling through output-length inflation and EOS correction. Hyperparameter interpretation now includes sampling-versus-greedy and POPE-versus-CHAIR tradeoffs. v2's explanation for restricting refinement to early layers disappears; limitations concerning attention-based causal relevance and visual grounding remain.

D1.justification: v3 documents revised alpha/gamma defaults, specifies top-p across sampling settings and identifies the LLaVA-OneVision checkpoint. However, it removes the explicit greater-than-70% co-occurrence selection threshold for the retained correlation analysis. The promised code-access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including ICT, Octopus, global/local attention assembly and DPO-based mitigation, while removing the O'Brien–Lewis contrastive-reasoning reference. The related-work taxonomy largely remains, with additional positioning around underexplored positional bias.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten around two failure mechanisms, method explanations are revised, and appendices are consolidated and reordered from A–G to A–E. Framework/module terminology changes throughout, alongside the title, author/affiliation block and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the introductory illustrations, redraws the method overview and adds positional-analysis displays. Main comparison tables are reorganized around additional backbones and decoding strategies. The detailed POPE table moves from main Table 1 to appendix Table 7; the qualitative caption figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, broader baseline/backbone comparisons, greedy evaluations and targeted positional controls strengthen support for applicability and design choices. Reporting problems limit the gain: the co-occurrence threshold is omitted, the new RoPE aliasing explanation lacks direct context-length validation, and CMPC's POPE F1 conflicts between v3 Tables 4 and 13 (85.70 versus 86.70).
